subject: Clarify per-token ladder, streaming rounding, and commit true-up
messages:
From: Emily Parson <emily.parson@brightroad.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on billable token rounding & streaming billing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked great for our live transcription flow. Before we move to a term sheet, procurement and engineering asked for a couple of clarifications on how Redwood meters usage for streaming sessions and how rounding is applied to per-token billing. Specifically: 

- For long-running streaming sessions (e.g., continuous transcription for telehealth visits lasting 40–90 minutes), how are tokens counted? Do you charge per incremental tokens generated, per-second checkpoints, or some other checkpointing method?
- If a stream sends very small increments (e.g., 3–8 tokens every 300ms), is there a rounding policy (nearest token, up to a bucket, per-utterance)?
- For commit tiers, do you count streaming tokens toward the same per-token ladder as request/response calls or is there a separate bucket for streaming?

I've attached a small sample of our usage logs (usage-logs-sample.csv) so you can see the pattern. Procurement asked that any rounding/aggregation rules be explicit in the term sheet so they can model spend.

Can you send proposed contract language or an appendix that spells out the metric definitions and examples? Kyle (our outside counsel) and our procurement team are cc'd.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Parson
Head of ML Product, BrightRoad Health
emily.parson@brightroad.com

Attachment: usage-logs-sample.csv (CSV, 32KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Parson <emily.parson@brightroad.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on billable token rounding & streaming billing

Hi Emily — great context and thank you for the sample. Looping in Ben (sales lead) and Laura (contracts) so we can give both an operational and legal view.

High level proposal we typically use for streaming-heavy customers (can be tailored):

1) Billable unit: billable_token = generated_tokens + consumed_prompt_tokens (same metric as hosted API).
2) Streaming checkpointing: to avoid high-frequency micro-billing we aggregate streaming tokens into 30-second checkpoints by default. Each checkpoint sums tokens emitted during the interval and then applies the billable_token rule above.
   - Example: 40 tokens over three partials in 30s -> checkpoint = 40 tokens billed.
3) Rounding: checkpoints are rounded up to the nearest 10 tokens for billing purposes (min rounding unit = 10).
   - So an aggregated checkpoint of 3 tokens -> billed as 10 tokens; 10 -> 10; 21 -> 30.
4) Commit tiers: streaming tokens count toward the same per-token ladder as standard API calls (no separate stream SKU). Commit true-up is monthly; excess usage draws from overage rates or moves you to the next tier if sustained.
5) Idle connection handling: we only bill checkpoints where tokens > 0. Idle durations with no token generation are not billed.

Attached is a draft appendix and a term sheet extract that tries to make the language unambiguous (Redwood_Termsheet_v3.pdf and usage-metrics-appendix.xlsx). Laura: below is suggested contract text we can drop into the SOW/appendix.

--- suggested contract snippet ---
"Billable Units and Streaming Metering
1. Definitions: 
   a) 'Token' means the smallest discrete text generation unit produced or consumed by the Service. 
   b) 'Billable Token' means the sum of tokens generated by Redwood models and prompt tokens consumed by Customer requests.
2. Streaming Sessions: 
   a) Redwood aggregates tokens produced by an active streaming session into fixed 30-second checkpoints. 
   b) For each checkpoint, Billable Tokens are summed and rounded up to the nearest 10 tokens for invoicing.
3. Commit & True-Up: 
   a) All Billable Tokens (streaming and non-streaming) roll up to the Customer's committed tier for the applicable billing period. Monthly true-up will reconcile usage against commit and apply overage or tier-adjustment credits as specified in the Pricing Annex."
--- end snippet ---

If that approach looks reasonable I can ask Legal to include it in a redline. Happy to change checkpoint window (15s/60s) or the rounding unit if you have a different modeling preference.

Sooj

Attachment: Redwood_Termsheet_v3.pdf, usage-metrics-appendix.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Emily Parson <emily.parson@brightroad.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, procurement@brightroad.com, Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@outsidelegal.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on billable token rounding & streaming billing

Thanks Emily and team — appreciate the detailed logs. Quick notes from Sales:

- We're happy to default to Soojin's 30s checkpoint + nearest-10 rounding; that gives BrightRoad predictable per-minute averages for modeling.
- Proposed alternative (if you prefer less rounding distortion): 15s checkpoints with rounding to nearest 5 tokens. This reduces overpay for micro-turns but increases the number of checkpoints.
- Commit economics: tokens streamed count toward committed volume. We'll do a monthly true-up and, if monthly usage consistently exceeds commit by >15% over 3 consecutive months, we'll trigger a review for an upward tier (optional automatic uplift only by written agreement).

Laura — from a contract drafting perspective, please add a short example table (2–3 rows) in the Pricing Annex that shows sample sessions and billed tokens for clarity for procurement.

Emily — if procurement and legal are comfortable with the 30s/10-token default, we can circulate a redline of the term sheet and provide a short modeling worksheet showing expected spend under both checkpoint options.

2) Add a one-line clarifier that idle open connections with zero tokens are never billed (so we avoid accidental socket charges).
